This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption with liftoff starting around 2026-10-29T07:36Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The footpoints extend from about S20W20 to S10W50. Post eruptive dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 with an opening of field lines seen over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Very minor and faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a very minor eruption from the former AR 14561 (S10W130) starting ~2026-10-30T11:25Z as seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. AR 14561 rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-10-27.

cmeAnalyses.note: An approximate analysis based on the location of the (very minor) source and the imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 coronagraphs and not confirmed by triangulation since the front is not seen in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-31T05:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2, as it may be obscured by the pylon or too faint to view clearly. The source of this event is an eruption from former AR 14561 (S11W140) beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T04:30Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195. Brightening near the region and dimming extending Northward can be seen in association with this eruption, possibly suggesting a Northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Diffuse CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T00:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen centered at approx. S15E65 beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T23:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193. This eruption is in close proximity to a coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T19:00Z. The CME is also visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. N15W15. Filament destabilization began at approx. 2026-11-01T16:43Z, with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T17:54Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement are also visible in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and one frame usable frame of STEREO A COR2, noting poor quality COR2 imagery affecting front visibility beyond one frame into a real-time data gap starting 2026-11-01T19:38Z.

data.note: Slow developing CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2, also observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR due to a data gap in real-time starting at 2026-11-01T19:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the NE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T18:14Z as filament ejecta and very wide, slow field line movement. An initial faint CME at 2026-11-01T18:36Z (LASCO C2) measuring plane-of-sky ~164 km/s is observed prior to this brighter emerging front.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only plane-of-sky with no STEREO A COR2 available to triangulate the far-sided source. This front starts very slow and speeds up, altering its shape slightly with a faster nose emerging in later frames; this behavior aligns with the GOES SUVI observed erupting field line activity.
Updated measurement with later frames of STEREO A COR2 to provide a 3D longitude fit.

data.note: Wide, slow CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-03T18:36Z. This CME is very slow to erupt, speeding up well after its first observation in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 starting loosely around 2026-11-03T08:00Z as wide, slow field line movement lasting several hours on/near the E limb, and source may be slightly far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 plane-of-sky using only later frames, as the front speeds up following most early frames.
Updated measurement using late frames of STEREO A COR2 to provide a 3D fit.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-04T02:48Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2, and is therefore not visible in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C3. This CME and source are also obscured by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2026-11-03T18:23Z to 2026-11-04T04:23Z. The source of this event is field line movement seen beyond the NW limb beginning at approx. 2026-11-04T02:00Z as seen in SOD AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source beyond the NE limb and lack of available STEREO A COR2 imagery for a 3D fit.

data.note: CME faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is unclear, but may be a small eruption seen near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 as an ejecta of material starting around 2026-11-05T03:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery as well as the potential source location.

data.note: CME faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME seen in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME first seen in white light imagery to the E in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-05T20:00Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like related to an M3.5 class flare from AR 14566 (S08E35) which peaked at 2026-11-05T18:33Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Some post-eruptive dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. Due to the source location being in close proximity to a coronal hole, some deflection is likely.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement based only on running difference imagery from GOES CCOR-1. This measurement is based on the source location, but there is a high degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the single perspective and the close proximity of the source to a coronal hole.

Updated measurement following a backfill in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 data. This measurement is based on the source location. Deflection to the East is possible for this CME due to its proximity to a coronal hole.

data.note: CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-05T14:35Z to 2026-11-06T01:38Z. The potential source location may be a minor eruption seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-05T19:28Z located near S15E75. Moving/opening field lines are also best seen in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Due to the faintness of the CME's leading edge in STEREO A COR2, there may be more uncertainty than usual in this measurement.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may possibly be a minor eruption starting around 2026-11-06T00:22Z in as best seen in SDO AIA 193, with moving field lines seen around S15E70.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery is not available due to a downlink data gap. The potential source is an eruption seen near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195/304 located around N20W160 starting around 2026-11-06T03:15Z. The eruption can be seen as an ejecta of material in STEREO A EUV 304. Moving field lines and post-eruption arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME may be faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2  at the time of the analysis, but was not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real time due to a downlink data gap. The source is an eruption just on or beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery seen as opening field lines starting at 2026-11-06T06:16Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Only two frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery were available for a measurement. The majority of the fit uses GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

data.note: Wide CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-06T13:38Z. The likely source is a filament eruption that starts to lift off in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery, around N35W140, starting at 2026-11-06T13:15Z. The filament can also be seen lifting off beyond the west limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.  Moving/opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location using GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery.

Measurement of the wider, fainter, potential shock feature of the CME. This shock feature appears to move more eastward than the leading edge and bulk of the CME as seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. STEREO A COR2 imagery was not available, so this measurement is approximate.

data.note: A very minor CME see to the NW in LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen STEREO A COR2 as there is a data gap. It is possible that this CME is an outflow following the 2026-11-06T16:15Z CME. No clear source for this CME has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME imagery is only available in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and is covered by a long data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source for this minor CME has not been found. Therefore only a plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely field line movement on/near the high latitude NE limb, observed starting around 2026-11-07T03:55Z in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting a deflected front making tracking with the swpc_cat tool difficult.

data.note: First in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, followed by slower CME 2026-11-07T10:24Z.  This leading edge is more faint and observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Second in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, following faster CME 2026-11-07T09:36Z.  This leading edge is brighter and observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z. This second CME is likely delayed filament material following the main eruption, observed deflecting eastward in GOES SUVI 304 and exiting the field-of-view by 2026-11-07T12:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2026-11-07T21:12Z. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be a filament eruption seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting at 2026-11-07T15:45Z. The eruption can also be seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of GOES SUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No source is observed in EUV imagery and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be further far-sided or observed as field line movement on the W limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 starting around 2026-11-08T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2. The source may be faint field line movement on or slightly beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 171 around 2026-11-09T07:06Z. This front is followed by a faint, slow, wide structure measuring approximately 122 km/s plane-of-sky, which may also be related to this eruption or separate far-sided, without current STEREO A COR2 to help differentiate.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as the CME is difficult to resolve in running difference LASCO C3 or not yet observed with available frames.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W only in STEREO A COR2 before a data gap begins at 2026-11-09T11:38Z, or in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 at all. No source is observed for this CME in available imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 plane-of-sky taken at W161.4 with STEREO A currently at W71.4. Only 4 available frames of the already faint front are usable before a data gap at 2026-11-09T11:38Z, and other coronagraphs do not observe this front.

data.note: Faint, narrow CME observed to the W only in GOES CCOR-1, due to a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption from AR 14571 starting around 2026-11-09T15:57Z, observed as dimming and brightening in SDO AIA 193 and field line movement in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only 3D fit to the observed source at W65, as such parameters may vary slightly. CME half with is slightly less than 10 degrees, limited by swpc_cat analysis tool.

data.note: Thin, faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, very faint in LASCO C2 and not observed in available STEREO A COR2 imagery. No distinct source is observed for this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

data.note: Wide, diffuse CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No distinct source observation or timing is observed beyond broad, slow, near-background movement of field lines in the SE quadrant of GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2026-11-10T17:00Z well before the first CME observation in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The streamer blowout may speed up to reanalyze later, but if not this analysis is considered final.

data.note: Thin, faint CME observed to the W in GOES CCOR-1 (partially obscured by earthshine) and STEREO A COR2, also in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after a data gap spanning approx. 2026-11-10T03:00Z - 2026-11-10T07:24Z. The source is AR 14571, with field line movement, brightening, and some small filament ejecta in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-11-10T03:56Z and centered ~S17W72.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, finding significant deflection westward to ~W90-W100 from the source observed at W72.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-11T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-11-11T12:23Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen originating from Active Region 14565 (N14W86) in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-11-11T22:55Z. This AR is in close proximity to a large coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 following a real-time data gap that ended at 2026-11-12T01:53Z. The source may be related to some "flickering" seen beyond the WSW limb in STA EUVI after a real-time data gap ending at 2026-11-12T01:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and single coronagraph view.
